hero.headline: Juno Beach faces fence dispute at JB-7 beach access that could cost thousands
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
hero.body:
A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point has created conflict between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with repairs potentially costing the town significant money. Residents at the Colony Condos report that people using the JB-7 public walkway have been crossing through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. With only bushes now separating the public access path from private land, the boundary between public and private areas has become unclear to visitors.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, explained that the problem intensifies during summer months when beachgoers arrive in large numbers. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." She noted that residents previously tried confronting trespassers directly but stopped after encounters became hostile. Now, the residents call police to handle the situation instead.

Not all beachgoers acknowledge a significant problem. Michael House, who regularly walks to JB-7 from a nearby public parking lot, said he has not observed the trespassing issues described by residents. "There's plenty of free parking. If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue," House said. "I have never noticed anyone hopping the fence or the shrubs or anything like that."

The issue reached the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where officials clarified that the town has no legal obligation to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring more affordable alternatives rather than reinstalling the original fence. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. Hill expressed hope that the town would take action to restore the boundary. "We're really hoping that the town will get back on board and just put it back up, so that we can have our landscaping and our private parking," Hill said. The council agreed to address the fence question during its budget discussions scheduled for July 15.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated Friday after prominent former DeSantis administration officials alleged they were operated by Layla Collins, wife .
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations emerged that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both identified online evidence connecting the accounts to the Second Lady. Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, triggered when someone attempts to access an account without the preset password. The screenshots showed an attempt to access the account triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits showing. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw said the account content suggested it existed entirely to advance Jay Collins' political ambitions in the Governor's race. The account posted only two types of content: promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the Governor. Redfern confirmed the allegations, stating the FSUDude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after the public accusations. Florida Politics has requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is deploying two boats with medics on standby this Fourth of July weekend as hundreds of boaters are expected to hit local .
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. The Martin County Maritime Response Unit is deploying two boats with medics on standby, stationed in the north and south of the county to respond to emergencies. Lt. Brett Harry said the team is prepared to assist with incidents ranging from minor injuries like stubbed toes to serious medical events including cardiac emergencies and potential spinal injuries.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, prioritizing safety during the holiday weekend. Lt. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court brief Thursday challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court brief Thursday challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009. Theobald was suspended last year after posting Facebook comments that labeled conservative activist Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In the filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone made numerous findings that are not based upon competent substantial evidence. The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a serious offense and that removing him was appropriate.

Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site
cards.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid proposal to transform 58 acres of stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district centered on a 13-acre civic park and permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch has chosen The Burg Bid as the city's preferred development plan for transforming Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District into a mixed-use neighborhood. Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, the $8.1 billion proposal centers on creating housing, hotels, offices, retail, cultural institutions, and entertainment spaces across the stadium site and surrounding public land. The development team will purchase 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with a $20 million deposit due when a purchase and sale agreement is finalized. Including $130 million in land the city will retain, the full land package is valued at $405 million.

The plan departs significantly from previous stadium-focused proposals by organizing development around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic space that would anchor the district. This central park would be part of 18.5 acres of public green space and would house The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, playgrounds, splash pads, event lawns, a concert venue, and public art installations. A Legacy Link pedestrian corridor will connect City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District. Additional amenities include a surf wave attraction, recreation deck, multimodal transportation hub, workforce training center, and a Resilience Event Center. The plan also addresses environmental restoration by reviving Booker Creek, which once served as a central feature of the Historic Gas Plant neighborhood before becoming a drainage ditch between the stadium and parking lots.

The proposal incorporates significant respect for the community history of the Gas Plant District, a predominantly Black neighborhood that was demolished to make way for Tropicana Field. The plan preserves the original gas tank footprint within Samuel Davis Park and weaves historic references throughout the district. Nine planned bridges over Booker Creek reference the nine bridges that once existed in the Historic Gas Plant area, symbolizing restoration of physical connections across the neighborhood. CEO Thompson Whitney Blake stated the team created "an evocative, architecturally jaw dropping permanent home for the Woodson African American Museum of Florida" and designed a Legacy Link that "rests on respect for the community that once existed here, informing and educating the future generations."

The development will occur in three five-year phases, with construction potentially beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before the stadium's demolition. The Tampa Bay Rays' lease with the city ends after the 2028 season. Phase 1 will establish cultural and workforce anchors including the Woodson and the Collaboratorium, a workforce training and business development center. Phase 2 will develop mixed-income neighborhoods and strengthen connections with surrounding districts. Phase 3 will complete the district as a regional cultural and events destination, including the 4,000 to 5,000-seat Resilience Event Center, which would also function as a hurricane evacuation shelter. The plan calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over the 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 at complementary sites throughout St. Petersburg.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman died in Monday home fire, friends fundraise for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed the couple's belongings.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office suggest an electrical issue may have caused the fire, though investigators continue their examination of the incident.

Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, learned of the tragedy through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said. Fenn visited the scene in the days following the fire to process her grief and described what she witnessed. "It's completely a state of devastation," she said. Friends have organized a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild his life after the flames destroyed many belongings that he and White shared.

Fenn reflected on White's character and the qualities that made her special to those who knew her. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." The loss carries added significance because White's birthday was approaching on the Fourth of July. "Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July. So, she passed just a few days before her birthday," Fenn said.

The tragedy compounds existing grief for Mark. According to Fenn, Mark previously lost his only child, Jacob, in a separate tragedy. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically. So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said. Despite the profound loss, Fenn said White's memory will remain alive in the hearts of those closest to her. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Fourth of July fireworks scheduled across Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: Fireworks displays are planned across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast for Independence Day.
cards.body:
Multiple fireworks displays are scheduled for Saturday across the Treasure Coast region. The events mark the Fourth of July holiday.

Communities throughout the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast are hosting celebrations. Residents can attend fireworks shows in various locations across the area.

cards.headline: S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach jumps from C to A rating as Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row. S.D. Spady Elementary School made a dramatic leap from a C rating last year to an A this year.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, with 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, receiving "A" or "B" ratings. The district set a record with a 93.5 percent graduation rate, and 86 percent of seniors participated in college-level coursework, including Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma. Superintendent Mike Burke stated the achievement reflects the commitment and hard work of students, teachers, school leaders, support staff, families, and community partners.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year, becoming one of four district schools to improve from "C" to "A." Principal Rona Tata, who has spent 15 years as principal after serving five years as assistant principal, said the school had an "A" rating two years ago and narrowly missed a "B" rating last year by a few points. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. The other schools improving from "C" to "A" include Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4 percent this year, with ground beef and strawberries hit hardest
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The price increase reflects broader inflation affecting key cookout staples. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5 percent, while buns are up 7.7 percent. Strawberries experienced the steepest increase at 12.4 percent, attributed to a Florida frost that damaged crops. Ice cream prices are also up 5.3 percent compared to last year.

Not all cookout items have become more expensive. Potato prices have declined this year, offering savings for those planning potato chips or salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends strategies to manage costs during the holiday season. She emphasized the importance of comparing prices across stores to find the best deals and reducing food waste as key ways families can save money. Woroch stressed that meal planning is the most critical step to minimize waste.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities in the nation to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, stating "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." She added that winning the award brings back community pride and reinforces the city's positive momentum.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem denies coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage for reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. Her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, said the surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to the denial letter, the surgery involved a synthetic surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the treatment's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, is calling for insurance companies to reconsider their coverage policies. Billington uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago with Billington's assistance. Anthem stated that GalaFlex "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval, though the company noted Clark retains the right to appeal. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction after investigative reporting on patient denials.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to march at National Independence Day Parade in Washington
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march a full mile along the National Mall on July 4 at 10:30 a.m., representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those watching from home.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the pressure of performing for millions of people watching nationally. "There are millions, if not billions, of people watching," Cabezas said. "It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion." She also explained the physical demands of marching band, noting that students must play their instruments, breathe properly, and walk while maintaining consistent sound. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on the marching and timing of everything. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying "I have full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing and said it showcases how much the program has grown.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with his comments, which labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock closes July 6 for renovations projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. When finished, the project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation includes a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, the year-long closure is necessary. During construction, the city is accommodating businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock to continue boarding passengers. Kuyrkendall said modernizing and expanding the dock will be great for the city and for businesses operating from the facility.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie works to expand Midway Road and add Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is moving forward with plans to expand Midway Road and add a partial interchange to Florida's Turnpike. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between current Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, which is still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County to consider elevated self-driving transit from West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: A California-based autonomous transit company is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to the airport now known as President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present an elevated self-driving transit proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially reducing trip times between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays or intermediate stops.

Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of traditional light rail, which previous South Florida discussions estimated at $400 million to $500 million per mile. He emphasized fares would be transit-level pricing, not private rideshare rates. The proposal comes as residents report increasing congestion and expensive rideshare costs. Tuesday's meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal rather than approve construction. If commissioners move forward, a planning and design contract could potentially be awarded later this year.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. Riviera Beach was also the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has earned a prestigious national honor as one of only 10 communities across the United States selected to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city stands as the sole Florida recipient of this year's recognition. The award celebrates communities that unite residents, local government, businesses, and organizations to address community challenges and create meaningful, lasting improvements. City leaders presented Riviera Beach's civic engagement efforts at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where judges announced the city as a first-time winner. Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the recognition, stating that "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars."

Lawson credited the award to years of sustained effort aimed at revitalizing the city and enhancing residents' quality of life. He noted that residents are witnessing the community transformation that city leaders envisioned. The honor reflects an extended commitment to strengthening civic health, building trust between residents and local government, and enabling the community to directly influence the city's future direction. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson attributed the award to residents' dedication and involvement. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," Miller-Anderson said. "Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

The city's application emphasized multiple initiatives designed to boost civic participation and neighborhood development. The Riviera Beach Youth Council engages high school students in civic leadership and advocacy work. The Citizens Leadership Academy provides civic education with a 98% completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program awards mini-grants to longtime homeowners for essential repairs. City leaders described these programs as part of a larger commitment to treating civic engagement as an ongoing partnership involving government, residents, faith organizations, schools, and community groups. Miller-Anderson emphasized the city's innovative approach, saying the programs ensure residents feel connected to what is happening in their community.

The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and ranks among the nation's most respected civic honors. Officials in Riviera Beach believe the designation celebrates the city's progress while positioning the community for future opportunities and continued development. The award communicates to the nation that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration produces results and residents actively shape their community's future. The complete list of 2026 All-America City Award recipients includes Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach considers elevated autonomous transit connecting airport to downtown
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The elevated network would connect President Donald J. Trump International Airport to the convention center, nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Gettinger emphasized the service would be priced like public transit rather than rideshare and said the system would require local employees for operations and maintenance. Tuesday's meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation to nearly double capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock closes July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The year-long project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees and will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises will be allowed to build a gate at the non-floating section of the dock to continue boarding passengers during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the dock's current limitations can make weekends hectic when boats squeeze in to find spots. Boat captain Parker Fisher said the dock has needed work over the years and he is glad the city is putting money into it.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home she shared with her fiancé in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn said Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically, and the timing of White's death compounds his grief. White's birthday is the Fourth of July, so she passed just a few days before her birthday. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing the piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. "She loves kids; she loves people." Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied insurance coverage hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She decided to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the treatment's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. Last year, after investigative reporting by Katie LaGrone and photojournalist Matthew Apthorp shared breast cancer patients' stories of denial, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Anthem stated the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage" without FDA approval, though the company said Clark retains the right to appeal.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year, survey finds
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The survey points to inflation as the primary cause, with several items showing significant price increases. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%, while ice cream prices have risen 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples are more expensive this year. Potato prices are down, which benefits those planning to serve potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically by comparing stores to find the best deals for items on your grocery list. She emphasizes that the biggest way families can control costs is by cutting down on food waste, which begins with creating a meal plan.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are working through a rigorous summer training program as they aim for a state championship during the 2026 fall football season. Last year, the team finished with a 10-2 record and won their district title, but an early playoff exit in the second round has motivated the program to reach higher goals this year.

Head football coach Jimmy Robertson emphasized the strength of this year's senior class, noting that most of them have been with the program since middle school. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said. This continuity and experience within the senior leadership gives the program a strong foundation for advancement.

To compete at the next level, Saint Andrew's has intentionally scheduled more challenging opponents for the upcoming season. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind this strategy, saying the team wants to test itself against quality competition to attract new players to the program. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that advancing further in the playoffs is the real measure of success for the Scots. While winning the regular season is important, Whelche stressed that it means nothing without postseason success. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs," he said.

The demanding summer workout schedule serves as daily motivation for the team as they build toward the season. Senior Edmyer St. Jean noted that the daily grind of training gives players something to anticipate and pushes them to work harder so they can see positive results when the season begins. The Scots are collectively embracing the challenge ahead, with their veteran senior class leading the charge to take the program to new heights and ultimately compete for a state title.

Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, have a designated driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended for Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The school board filed a court document Thursday arguing that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending reinstatement of Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy.
cards.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended last year following social media comments that labeled Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the Martin County School Board argued against Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone's recommendation to reinstate Theobald, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. The school board retains the final authority on whether Theobald will be reinstated, with no timeline specified for a decision.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets roof fixed and lien removed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his roof but said the company left two holes unfinished and stopped responding to his calls.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said it left two holes unfinished on the back of his home. He attempted to contact the contractor multiple times between January 10 and February 5, including calls, texts and emails. One email from a worker on February 5 promised the owner would call him, but McCoy said the owner never did.

Letters from Gulfeagle Supply warned McCoy that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his home with the county. The lien stated that Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid for those supplies. After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the Seabreeze Roofing owner, who declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons, the situation quickly changed. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, lifting the lien from his property. About an hour later, McCoy sent WPTV a photo showing crews back on his roof finishing the work.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient and surgeon criticize insurance denial for reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage for breast reconstruction using GalaFlex mesh by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before her scheduled surgery.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery was scheduled, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving GalaFlex mesh is considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction, making it an off-label and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and believes insurance companies should reconsider their policies. While acknowledging no treatment is risk-free, Billington says the product is less risky than other options with proven success and represents "the gold standard in breast reconstruction with implants" based on published data. Despite the denial, Clark had her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. Anthem responded that it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they align with medical evidence and treatment standards, but the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage."

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during sea turtle nesting season through September. Available programs include guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The center designed these experiences to give visitors an opportunity to learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups encourage beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site
hero.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid proposal to transform 58 acres of stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district centered on a 13-acre civic park and permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
hero.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch has chosen The Burg Bid as the city's preferred development plan for transforming Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District into a mixed-use neighborhood. Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, the $8.1 billion proposal centers on creating housing, hotels, offices, retail, cultural institutions, and entertainment spaces across the stadium site and surrounding public land. The development team will purchase 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with a $20 million deposit due when a purchase and sale agreement is finalized. Including $130 million in land the city will retain, the full land package is valued at $405 million.

The plan departs significantly from previous stadium-focused proposals by organizing development around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic space that would anchor the district. This central park would be part of 18.5 acres of public green space and would house The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, playgrounds, splash pads, event lawns, a concert venue, and public art installations. A Legacy Link pedestrian corridor will connect City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District. Additional amenities include a surf wave attraction, recreation deck, multimodal transportation hub, workforce training center, and a Resilience Event Center. The plan also addresses environmental restoration by reviving Booker Creek, which once served as a central feature of the Historic Gas Plant neighborhood before becoming a drainage ditch between the stadium and parking lots.

The proposal incorporates significant respect for the community history of the Gas Plant District, a predominantly Black neighborhood that was demolished to make way for Tropicana Field. The plan preserves the original gas tank footprint within Samuel Davis Park and weaves historic references throughout the district. Nine planned bridges over Booker Creek reference the nine bridges that once existed in the Historic Gas Plant area, symbolizing restoration of physical connections across the neighborhood. CEO Thompson Whitney Blake stated the team created "an evocative, architecturally jaw dropping permanent home for the Woodson African American Museum of Florida" and designed a Legacy Link that "rests on respect for the community that once existed here, informing and educating the future generations."

The development will occur in three five-year phases, with construction potentially beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before the stadium's demolition. The Tampa Bay Rays' lease with the city ends after the 2028 season. Phase 1 will establish cultural and workforce anchors including the Woodson and the Collaboratorium, a workforce training and business development center. Phase 2 will develop mixed-income neighborhoods and strengthen connections with surrounding districts. Phase 3 will complete the district as a regional cultural and events destination, including the 4,000 to 5,000-seat Resilience Event Center, which would also function as a hurricane evacuation shelter. The plan calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over the 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 at complementary sites throughout St. Petersburg.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated Friday after prominent former DeSantis administration officials alleged they were operated by Layla Collins, wife .
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations emerged that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both identified online evidence connecting the accounts to the Second Lady. Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, triggered when someone attempts to access an account without the preset password. The screenshots showed an attempt to access the account triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and to a phone number with only the last digits showing. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw said the account content suggested it existed entirely to advance Jay Collins' political ambitions in the Governor's race. The account posted only two types of content: promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the Governor. Redfern confirmed the allegations, stating the FSUDude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after the public accusations. Florida Politics has requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Byrd seeks to keep GOP candidate Paula Stark off House District 47 ballot
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd asked a Leon Circuit Court to keep Paula Stark off the ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork before the June 12 qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to keep Republican Paula Stark off the House District 47 ballot, arguing she failed to submit required paperwork by the June 12 deadline. Stark's incomplete qualifying materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before noon on June 12. In his court response, Byrd said Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests. Five state employees gave sworn written declarations stating Davis never submitted the form nor was it accidentally handed back when he submitted other paperwork in the final qualifying hour. Three weeks after the deadline passed, Stark still had not submitted Form 6, according to Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve.

Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly turn in Form 6. Half of those candidates corrected the problems and still qualified. Reeve also noted Stark's treasurer filed a campaign finance report over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. Byrd said ballots must be mailed to overseas military by July 4 and vote-by-mail ballots are due out July 9-16. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47, representing Osceola and Orange counties, would feature Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves, with no other Republicans having filed.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman died in Monday home fire, friends fundraise for fiance
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed the couple's belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office suggest an electrical issue may have caused the fire, though investigators continue their examination of the incident.

Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, learned of the tragedy through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said. Fenn visited the scene in the days following the fire to process her grief and described what she witnessed. "It's completely a state of devastation," she said. Friends have organized a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild his life after the flames destroyed many belongings that he and White shared.

Fenn reflected on White's character and the qualities that made her special to those who knew her. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." The loss carries added significance because White's birthday was approaching on the Fourth of July. "Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July. So, she passed just a few days before her birthday," Fenn said.

The tragedy compounds existing grief for Mark. According to Fenn, Mark previously lost his only child, Jacob, in a separate tragedy. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically. So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said. Despite the profound loss, Fenn said White's memory will remain alive in the hearts of those closest to her. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

hero.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie
hero.teaser: Costco is planning to open its first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie.
hero.body:
The warehouse retailer is bringing its first store to the Treasure Coast with a planned location in Port St. Lucie. This marks the first Costco presence in the region and reflects the city's ongoing growth and development initiatives.

Port St. Lucie is experiencing significant infrastructure improvements to support this expansion and other commercial development. The city is working on a $95 million Midway Road Widening Project that aims to address congestion and safety concerns. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, "There's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie." The project is designed to accommodate both current needs and anticipated growth over the next several decades. Crews are currently in the first phase of the Midway Road project, widening the roadway from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will extend from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction expected to begin in Summer 2027.

Beyond the road widening work, transportation planners are also enhancing access to Florida's Turnpike. The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to dedicate 7 acres of city land to the Florida Department of Transportation to support a partial interchange on the Turnpike. Samples noted that this interchange is essential for accessibility and growth management, stating "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years." The partial interchange is still in the design phase. The city council will vote on final approval of the land dedication at an upcoming meeting. FDOT is also working to improve the Turnpike bridge as part of these broader improvements.

The infrastructure investments extend beyond major roadways. The Midway Road Widening Project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks to improve connectivity throughout the area. While construction activity has been noticeable to residents, the improvements are widely viewed as necessary for the city's future. Local resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged the disruption but expressed support, saying "We definitely needed it to be expanded" and noting that "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." These transportation enhancements position Port St. Lucie to accommodate major retail developments like Costco while supporting the community's continued growth trajectory.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances $95 million Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St.

Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike on Midway Road. The city council will vote on final approval at an upcoming meeting. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between the current entrances and exits to the Turnpike in Port St. Lucie and is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years. The partial interchange is still in the design phase, according to the FDOT website.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in summer 2027. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks, and FDOT is working on improving the Turnpike bridge.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs increase 4 percent this year
hero.teaser: Holiday meals for 10 people now cost $73.82, according to a national survey tracking cookout expenses.
hero.body:
The cost of hosting a Fourth of July cookout for 10 people has increased to $73.82 this year, representing a 4 percent rise from 2023, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The increase reflects broader inflationary pressures on holiday meal staples. Ground beef prices have climbed 5.5 percent, while buns have increased 7.7 percent. Strawberry prices surged 12.4 percent following a Florida frost that damaged crops. Ice cream prices also rose 5.3 percent compared to the previous year.

Not all cookout ingredients have become more expensive. Potato prices decreased this year, offering savings for shoppers planning potato chips or salads. Corn prices have fluctuated locally, though produce from the Glades can provide better deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommended strategies to manage holiday meal expenses, including comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for items on shopping lists and reducing food waste through meal planning.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient's insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her breast reconstruction surgery denied by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before the scheduled procedure.
cards.body:
Beth Clark was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure involving GalaFlex surgical mesh. According to the denial letter, the surgery is considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction, making it an off-label treatment.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the mesh about a week ago after Billington found an alternative mechanism to make it happen. An Anthem spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with the latest treatment standards, and that Clark has the right to appeal the decision. Last year, Cigna became the first major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction after investigative reporting on patient denials.
